# Direct rest-of-day forecast: does it trade better? (checklist E2)

*Generated by `experiments/restofday_trading_test.py`; every number below is read from the CSVs in this folder. Inputs: forecast tables `results/spxw_pnl/yhat_{restofday,sub}_*`, return ledger `results/linear_subsection_restofday/trading_test/dh_holdclose_ledger.parquet`, 15:30 identity flags `results/linear_subsection_restofday_dedup/score_rest_of_day.csv`.*

## Question

The direct rest-of-day model forecasts, at each entry time, the variance from that time to the 16:00 close in one regression per entry time. Its QLIKE beats the one-step construction (next-bar forecast stretched by the causal intraday profile, RVhat/w). Does it also make a better trading signal?

## Set-up (one change at a time)

- **Trade.** At each entry time (09:35, 10:00, ..., 15:30) buy or sell the straddle (nearest out-of-the-money call + nearest out-of-the-money put, same-day expiry, one position), hold it to the official close, delta-hedged in the index every 30 minutes (the hold-to-close notebook's section 4b). The 15:30 entry is the last-30-min trade. Midpoint and crossed-spread fills (buy at the ask, sell at the bid, cash settlement).
- **Rule.** sign(s): long the straddle when s > 0, short otherwise; flat on the 13 bars whose vendor implied volatility is a censored solver node (the same bars for every signal).
- **Signals.** s_current = RVhat/w - IV^2 h (the notebook's one-step construction) against s_direct = F_rem - IV^2 h (the direct forecast). IV is the vendor's hourly implied volatility of the straddle at entry, h the hours to the close. Same days, same bars, same fills, same hedge; only the forecast of the rest of the day changes.
- **Forecasts.** The per-bar linear models' three buckets: live-feasible, all features, HAR + calendar (`har_ma_*` and the calendar columns). Headline estimator: per-bar ridge; lasso and elastic net are in the CSVs.
- **Forecast level, two variants fixed before any trading number was computed.** *plain* (headline): the QLIKE comparison's own construction -- direct = pred_adj^2 x baseline_rem, current = the scorer's one-step F_rem = f_next / w_next. *recal*: both sides through the notebook's Mincer-Zarnowitz recalibration (250 prior sessions), fitted per entry time on that entry time's own target, current then divided by the same w.
- **Days.** The 15:30 deck's 866 expiration days (2020-01 .. 2024-04). Every forecast has a value on every bar, so no bar is dropped. 09:35 uses the forecasts issued at 09:30 (five minutes before entry, used as issued).
- **Intervals.** Paired circular block bootstrap of direct minus current on the same resampled days (block ceil(n^(1/3)), 2000 draws, seed 0; 95 % percentile, basic interval in the CSVs), the notebook's section 7 recipe.

## Answer: pooled over entry times 10:00-15:30 (daily sums; per-bar ridge, plain)

| bucket | current, mid | direct, mid | direct - current, mid [95 %] | current, crossed | direct, crossed | direct - current, crossed [95 %] | buy % current / direct | same sign % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| live-feasible | 2.12 | 2.49 | +0.37 [-0.38, +1.05] | 1.00 | 1.48 | +0.48 [-0.20, +1.20] | 43.6 / 37.6 | 76.3 |
| all features | 2.23 | 2.54 | +0.31 [-0.37, +0.97] | 1.13 | 1.58 | +0.45 [-0.19, +1.16] | 44.2 / 37.9 | 76.0 |
| HAR + calendar | 1.33 | 1.45 | +0.12 [-0.63, +0.85] | 0.20 | 0.40 | +0.20 [-0.51, +0.96] | 46.2 / 44.6 | 78.1 |

References on the same 866 days: always short 2.93 mid / 2.21 crossed; the notebook's block-diagonal ridge sign(s) 2.40 / 1.35 (reproduced to machine precision, see Checks).

**In one line.** With the live-feasible and all-features inputs the direct forecast trades somewhat better (+0.37 and +0.31 Sharpe pooled at the midpoint), mostly because it buys the straddle less often; no difference is distinguishable from zero, and neither signal beats always short.

**Reading.**

- With the live-feasible and all-features inputs the direct forecast trades better by a point estimate of +0.37 and +0.31 Sharpe at the midpoint (+0.48 and +0.45 at the crossed spread), but every one of these intervals includes zero. With HAR + calendar the two are level (+0.12).
- Across all 18 estimator x bucket x back-transform combinations (midpoint), the direct forecast is ahead in 15; intervals (percentile and basic both) exclude zero in favour of the direct forecast in 0 and against it in 0 (crossed: 0 and 0). 1 further row(s) have the percentile interval alone excluding zero: enet / all features / plain / crossed +0.70 [+0.07, +1.42]. The pooled forest plot (`trading_test_pooled_dsharpe.png`) shows them all.
- Neither signal beats always short (every pooled point estimate is below it): direct minus always short -0.44 [-2.02, +0.86] (live-feasible, mid), -0.40 [-1.99, +0.96] (all features), -1.49 [-3.25, +0.03] (HAR + calendar); current minus always short -0.81 [-2.41, +0.53], -0.70 [-2.33, +0.65], -1.61 [-3.31, -0.20].
- Hit rate (share of days with a positive daily sum, mid): live-feasible 0.560 current vs 0.572 direct; all features 0.554 vs 0.558; HAR + calendar 0.535 vs 0.522.

## By entry time (per-bar ridge, plain, midpoint)

- **live-feasible**: direct ahead at 9 of 12 entry times (09:35-15:00; 15:30 is the same forecast). Best 10:00: 0.53 -> 1.79, +1.26 [+0.13, +2.51]; worst 12:00: 0.84 -> 0.37, -0.47 [-1.60, +0.62]. Intervals excluding zero: in favour at 10:00, 15:00; against at none.
- **all features**: direct ahead at 9 of 12 entry times (09:35-15:00; 15:30 is the same forecast). Best 11:30: 0.11 -> 1.52, +1.41 [+0.29, +2.68]; worst 12:30: 1.54 -> 1.16, -0.39 [-1.33, +0.62]. Intervals excluding zero: in favour at 11:30; against at none.
- **HAR + calendar**: direct ahead at 7 of 12 entry times (09:35-15:00; 15:30 is the same forecast). Best 10:00: -0.07 -> 0.85, +0.92 [-0.07, +2.02]; worst 13:00: 1.47 -> 0.42, -1.04 [-2.01, -0.10]. Intervals excluding zero: in favour at none; against at 13:00.
- 4 of these 36 per-entry-time intervals exclude zero; at 95 % about 1.8 would by chance, so single entry times are not evidence on their own.
- Figure: `trading_test_sharpe_by_entry_time.png` (top: Sharpe by entry time, current vs direct with 95 % intervals, always short dashed; bottom: the paired difference).

## Why: the direct forecast buys less, and the buys lose

- **live-feasible**: buy share 43.6 % (current) vs 37.6 % (direct) over 10:00-15:30. Over 09:35-15:00 the signs differ on 2689 bars: 1654 where the direct forecast sells and the current one buys (mean hedged long-straddle return there -0.083 per unit premium) and 1035 the other way (-0.075). Direct minus current on those bars: +274.0 units of premium from the first group, -156.2 from the second, net +117.9 over the sample.
- **all features**: buy share 44.2 % (current) vs 37.9 % (direct) over 10:00-15:30. Over 09:35-15:00 the signs differ on 2732 bars: 1688 where the direct forecast sells and the current one buys (mean hedged long-straddle return there -0.095 per unit premium) and 1044 the other way (-0.092). Direct minus current on those bars: +321.3 units of premium from the first group, -192.1 from the second, net +129.2 over the sample.
- **HAR + calendar**: buy share 46.2 % (current) vs 44.6 % (direct) over 10:00-15:30. Over 09:35-15:00 the signs differ on 2495 bars: 1309 where the direct forecast sells and the current one buys (mean hedged long-straddle return there -0.090 per unit premium) and 1186 the other way (-0.077). Direct minus current on those bars: +236.9 units of premium from the first group, -183.7 from the second, net +53.2 over the sample.

On the bars where the two disagree the long straddle loses on average in both directions, so whichever signal sells there gains, by about the same amount per bar in either group. The direct forecast sits lower against the quoted implied variance and so lands in the first group more often; that, not better timing of its buys, is where its point gain comes from. It is the mirror image of the notebook's section 8d, where fitted rest-of-day maps sat higher, bought more, and traded worse (executed notebook, pooled 10:00-15:00, block-diagonal ridge):

| rule (section 8d) | Sharpe mid | Sharpe crossed | buy % |
|---|---|---|---|
| always short | 3.38 | 2.65 | 0.0 |
| sign(s^m) | 2.30 | 1.25 | 38.6 |
| sign(s^rem) M1 | 1.70 | 0.68 | 46.6 |
| sign(s^rem) M2 | 1.15 | 0.22 | 48.3 |
| sign(s^rem) M3 | 0.86 | -0.07 | 48.4 |

On the same 10:00-15:00 pool the direct forecast (per-bar ridge, plain) has live-feasible 2.27 mid / 1.26 crossed (current 1.82 / 0.68); all features 2.35 mid / 1.39 crossed (current 1.96 / 0.83); HAR + calendar 1.18 mid / 0.16 crossed (current 1.05 / -0.09).

## QLIKE gains and trading gains

On these bars the direct forecast's pooled QLIKE (10:00-15:30, against the realized rest of the day) is lower than the one-step's by 26.6 % (live-feasible), 62.1 % (all features), 18.1 % (HAR + calendar) with the plain back-transform and by 37.5 %, 36.4 %, 18.6 % recalibrated (the plain all-features figure is inflated by the one-step's extreme values, below). With the plain back-transform the trade moves the same way as QLIKE in all three buckets; recalibrated, it reverses for HAR + calendar; either way the trading difference is small next to its sampling error. Earlier comparisons already showed QLIKE and the trade parting ways (the VIX-only forecast in the RV-IV notebook; the fitted rest-of-day maps of section 8d). A better forecast of the rest-of-day variance is not the same thing as a better sign of s: the sign depends on where the forecast sits against the implied variance on the marginal days.

## The recalibrated variant (robustness)

| bucket | current, mid | direct, mid | direct - current [95 %] | direct - current, crossed [95 %] | buy % current / direct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| live-feasible | 1.40 | 1.82 | +0.42 [-0.30, +1.18] | +0.55 [-0.14, +1.39] | 52.4 / 45.6 |
| all features | 1.33 | 1.81 | +0.48 [-0.25, +1.28] | +0.65 [-0.06, +1.53] | 52.4 / 46.3 |
| HAR + calendar | 0.41 | 0.21 | -0.20 [-1.00, +0.60] | -0.10 [-0.85, +0.72] | 53.7 / 54.9 |

The recalibration adds the error-variance term and lifts both forecasts (median plain / recalibrated live-feasible direct 0.950, live-feasible current 0.937, all features direct 0.939, all features current 0.940, HAR + calendar direct 0.940, HAR + calendar current 0.949), and both buy more; both trade worse than plain, and the ordering of direct against current is the same as under plain for live-feasible and all features and reverses (inside the interval) for HAR + calendar. Positions that differ between plain and recal (ridge): live-feasible direct 1213, live-feasible current 1192, all features direct 1264, all features current 1090, HAR + calendar direct 1268, HAR + calendar current 1006 of 11250 bars.

**Extreme values of the plain back-transform.** sign(s) uses only the sign of s, so a single extreme forecast moves one position, not the size of any trade. On this frame the largest realized / plain forecast ratio (the tail that drives QLIKE) is live-feasible direct 265, live-feasible current 131, all features direct 141, all features current 1956, HAR + calendar direct 28, HAR + calendar current 45; the recal variant is the check on them.

## Checks

```
inputs: forecast tables results/spxw_pnl/yhat_{restofday,sub}_*; ledger results/linear_subsection_restofday/trading_test/dh_holdclose_ledger.parquet
GATE join: the direct tables' realized rest of day equals the per-bar tables' bars summed from the entry time to the close on every bar of all 9 models (max rel 9.6e-13); the realized target is the same in every direct table
bars without every forecast (dropped from every rule): 0 of 11250
frame: 11,250 bars, 866 days; days per entry time {'09:35': 863, '10:00': 864, '10:30': 865, '11:00': 865, '11:30': 865, '12:00': 866, '12:30': 866, '13:00': 866, '13:30': 866, '14:00': 866, '14:30': 866, '15:00': 866, '15:30': 866}
bars with a censored vendor implied volatility (flat in every sign rule): 13
15:30 identity flags read from results/linear_subsection_restofday_dedup/score_rest_of_day.csv
GATE 15:30: direct F = one-step F (rel <= 1e-09, same position) on all 866 days wherever the scorer's identity self-check passes; where it fails:
Empty DataFrame
Columns: [estimator, bucket, variant, scorer identity_pass, max rel |F_direct/F_current - 1| at 15:30, 15:30 days whose position differs]
Index: []
GATE the notebook's always short and block-diagonal ridge sign(s), recomputed on this frame (10,387 bars 10:00-15:30), equal its pooled mid / crossed and per-entry-time Sharpe (max |diff| 4.4e-16)
```

## What this does not settle

- One sample, 2020-01 .. 2024-04; the per-entry-time intervals are wide and a dozen of them are looked at.
- The 09:35 forecasts cover 09:30-16:00 while the straddle covers 09:35-16:00 (used as issued on both sides).
- Sizing: every rule is +/-1 unit of premium per entry time; the size question is A3's.
